note: v1: FIRST LIGHT, the album's door: 2-step liquid drum & bass, dawn into the dancefloor. UK-garage 2-step at 174 is its identity (a kick on the one and a skip on the and-of-3, the snare on 2 and 4 with ghosts, sixteenth hats swung like garage), with a quiet bed of wM's amen re-sequenced from its ghost slices rolling underneath. Euphoria and melancholy share the same four chords (Abmaj9 Gm9 Cm9 Bb13sus) on a juno pad and an epiano comping in the 2-step's gaps; a warm 808 sub on the roots; a short vocal-chop hook (G Eb F G | Bb G F Eb) from a tape voice through a formant filter, made bigger with formant-preserving pitch; a soft drifting reese only in the second drop. Patient (Harry's direction): it opens drumless and half-time in tape hiss and lets the 2-step in through an opening filter. LEVELS first, after Harry's clipped-bass note: the engine's limiter flat-tops whenever it acts, so the drum bus is clipped and a smooth fast peak compressor sits in front of the limiter; true peak -1.6 dBTP, flat runs 5 / 3 samples (seeds 0/11), at the cost of loudness (-16.7 LUFS) until wM's limiter fix lands. Seeds 0/11: 74.67 / 72.44 (master 16: rms -19.5 below the album band; spectrum 59: too much top).
next: Spectrum (too much air above 10 kHz); loudness up once the limiter is fixed; agree the album loudness target; Harry's notes.
